purpose: Metreleptin is used to treat a rare condition called generalized lipodystrophy, where the body has little to no fat tissue. Because of this, the body cannot make enough of a hormone called leptin, which helps control hunger and metabolism. This medicine helps replace that missing leptin so your body can work more normally.
how_it_works: Leptin is a natural hormone your body makes in fat cells that helps regulate how you eat, store energy, and manage blood sugar. In lipodystrophy, you do not have enough fat cells, so your body does not make enough leptin. Metreleptin is a man-made version of leptin that you inject under your skin to make up for what your body is missing.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include low blood sugar (especially if you take insulin or diabetes medicines), headache, weight loss, stomach pain, and reactions at the injection site such as redness or bruising. Some people may also feel tired or develop ear infections.
warnings: This medicine carries a serious warning because it may cause the immune system to make antibodies that block not only this medicine but also your body's own leptin, which could make your condition worse. There is also a risk of a rare but serious blood cancer called T-cell lymphoma, so your doctor will monitor you closely. This medicine is only available through a special restricted program called the Myalept REMS Program, meaning your doctor must be enrolled to prescribe it.
typical_dosing: Metreleptin is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous) once daily. The dose is based on your body weight. For adults and children weighing more than 40 kg (about 88 lbs), the starting dose is typically 2.5 mg for females and 2.5 mg for males, adjusted as needed. Your healthcare team will teach you how to inject it properly and help you find the right dose for you.
